records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: The Law of the Republic of Tajikistan “On the National Bank of Tajikistan”, No. 722 of 28 June 2011, signed by President Emomali Rahmon, puts every seat on the bank's Board in the President's hands. Article 74(4) says the Chairman of the National Bank and his deputies are appointed to office and released from office by decree of the President, with the decrees submitted to the lower house of parliament for approval, and article 74(3) says the Board's three independent members are approved by the President on the Chairman's proposal. Article 74(6) says the President sets the salary of the Chairman and his deputies.
records.source_title: Закон Республики Таджикистан «О Национальном банке Таджикистана», 28 июня 2011 года № 722 (Individuals' Deposit Insurance Fund of Tajikistan)
records.quote: Председатель Национального банка Таджикистана и его заместители назначаются на должность и освобождаются от должности Указом Президента Республики Таджикистан

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: Syria's Basic Monetary Law No. 23 of 2002, issued in Damascus on 17 March 2002 by President Bashar al-Assad, places the bank and its policy-making council under the government. Article 1 says the Monetary and Credit Council works within the general economic directions of the state approved by the Council of Ministers, and sets monetary policy in line with the state's general strategy. Article 8(3) says the Council's decisions are communicated to the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade, who may suspend for up to seven days any decision he considers contrary to the interest of the state, and if the disagreement continues he must refer the matter to the Council of Ministers to decide. Article 69 says the Governor is appointed, and his service terminated, by decree; article 2 puts the Council's non-bank seats, among them assistant ministers of economy, finance, agriculture and industry and the head of the State Planning Authority, in the gift of a decree on their ministries' proposal; and article 71 says the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade names the four supervising directors who sit with the Governor on the management committee.
records.source_title: قانون النقد الأساسي — القانون رقم 23 لعام 2002 (Central Bank of Syria)
records.quote: يجري تعيين الحاكم وإنهاء خدمته وتحديد راتبه وتعويضاته بمرسوم

parties.role: approves the economic directions the bank's council must work within and decides disputed council decisions

parties.party: Ministry of Economy and Foreign Trade of Syria
parties.role: may suspend the bank council's decisions and names the bank's supervising directors

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: Bermuda's monetary authority is run by a board the finance minister appoints and can be told what to do by him. The Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969 (1969:57), in the consolidated text the Authority publishes, says at section 21(2) that the Minister may give the Authority written general directions that appear to him necessary in the public interest, and that the Authority shall act in accordance with them. Section 4(1)(d) says eleven members of the Board are appointed by the Minister, section 4E(1) says the Minister appoints the Chairman, and section 4E(6) lets the Minister terminate the Chairman's appointment if satisfied he is unable or unfit to discharge his functions. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
records.source_title: Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969 (Bermuda Monetary Authority)
records.quote: The Minister may from time to time, after consultation with the Authority, give to the Authority in writing such general directions as appear to the Minister to be necessary in the public interest and the Authority shall act in accordance with such directions.

parties.role: may give the Authority binding directions and appoints its chairman and most of its board

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: The Cayman Islands Monetary Authority Law (2020 Revision), revised as at 31 December 2019 and still the principal Act after the Monetary Authority (Amendment and Validation) Act 2024 changed only its fees and regulation-making sections, puts the Authority under the Cabinet. Section 33(1) says the Cabinet may give the Authority written general directions that appear to it necessary in the public interest, and the Authority shall act in accordance with them. Section 12(1) says the Cabinet appoints the directors, section 11(3) says it designates the chairperson and deputy chairperson, section 13(1) says it appoints the managing director, and section 14(3) says the Cabinet, in the public interest, may terminate the appointment of any director. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
records.source_title: Monetary Authority Law (2020 Revision) (Cayman Islands Monetary Authority)
records.quote: The Cabinet may, from time to time, after consultation with the board, give to the Authority, in writing, such general directions as appear to the Cabinet to be necessary in the public interest

parties.role: may give the Authority binding directions and appoints and may remove its directors

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: Under the Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012, which the bank publishes, section 37 says the Minister for Finance may, with the approval of Cabinet, give the Central Bank written directions where the Minister is of the opinion that coordination of monetary and fiscal policies or the public interest requires it, and must publish those directions in the Gazette and lay them before Parliament. Section 41(3) says the other directors of the Board are appointed by the Minister after consultation with the Governor, and section 41(1) says the Governor is appointed by the Governor-General on Cabinet's recommendation. Under section 44 the Governor, Deputy Governor and other Board members may be removed before their term ends only on grounds of permanent incapacity or serious misconduct, and the Governor only on a tribunal's recommendation. The Central Bank of Solomon Islands (Amendment) Act 2023 does not amend sections 37, 41 or 44. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
records.source_title: Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012 (Central Bank of Solomon Islands)
records.quote: may, with the approval of Cabinet, give the Central Bank in writing such directions where the Minister is of the opinion that coordination of monetary and fiscal policies or public interest requires to do so

parties.party: Minister for Finance of Solomon Islands
parties.role: may give the bank written directions with Cabinet approval and appoints its non-executive directors
approves the directions given to the bank and recommends the Governor's appointment

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: The National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, Chapter 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition, puts the bank's board in the government's hands and gives Cabinet the last word on policy disputes. Section 10(1) says the Minister, with the consent of Cabinet, appoints five directors and appoints the Chairman and Deputy Chairman; section 11(1) says the Governor is appointed by Cabinet on the Minister's recommendation; and section 11(3) says the Governor may be removed from office by Cabinet, on the Minister's recommendation made at the Board's request, for permanent incapacity, serious misconduct or failure to perform his duties. Section 50(1) says the Minister may, with the consent of Cabinet, issue the bank written directives, and section 50(4) says that where the Minister and the Board disagree about a policy the Board has determined, the Minister must submit the disagreement to Cabinet to determine the policy to be adopted by the bank. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
records.source_title: National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, CAP. 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition (Attorney General's Office, Tonga)
records.quote: The Minister upon receipt of a statement of the difference of opinion from the Board shall forthwith submit it to Cabinet within 7 days of receipt to determine the policy in relation to that difference of opinion to be adopted by the Bank.

parties.role: appoints and may remove the bank's governor and directors and determines policy where it disagrees with the board
appoints directors with Cabinet consent and may issue the bank written directives

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
records.summary: Aruba's Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), as amended through AB 2014 no. 5 and published by the Centrale Bank van Aruba in Dutch and in the bank's English translation, keeps the bank under the Governor of Aruba and the Minister of Finance. Section 18 says the president and executive directors are appointed by the Governor from a shortlist of three put up by the Supervisory Board, and that the Governor may suspend or dismiss them by state decree. Section 19(3) says general guidelines for the performance of the duties of the president and executive directors can be set out in a state decree. Section 23 says the chairman of the Supervisory Board is the Government Commissioner, appointed and dismissed by the Governor, that the other supervisory directors are appointed by the Governor, and that they may be suspended or dismissed before the end of their term by the Governor. Section 27(1) says the Government Commissioner supervises the bank's activities on behalf of the Country and acts in accordance with general or specific instructions given by the Minister. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
records.source_title: Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), English translation (Centrale Bank van Aruba)
records.quote: The Government Commissioner supervises the Bank's activities on behalf of the Country and in doing so will act in accordance with general or specific instructions given by the Minister.

parties.role: appoints, suspends and dismisses the bank's president, directors and supervisory board
instructs the government commissioner who oversees the bank and chairs its supervisory board

records.summary: Central Banking reported that government officials removed Reserve Bank of Fiji governor Savenaca Narube and replaced him with deputy governor Sada Reddy, hours before the Fiji dollar was devalued by 20%. The report says the new government had come to power the previous week and was led by the army. No official reason for the removal is given; the report notes Narube had recently warned about the economy and forecast a 0.3% contraction for 2009.
records.source_title: Fiji sacks Narube and devalues dollar (Central Banking)
records.quote: occupied the central bank and replaced Narube

records.summary: Diario El Mundo reported that Nicolás Martínez, president of the Banco Central de Reserva, answered a summons from a Legislative Assembly commission investigating the debt the government had taken on and how it was used during the COVID-19 pandemic, and resigned the day after appearing. Deputies asked him whether the release of banks' liquidity reserve was designed so banks could buy Treasury paper; he answered that it was an autonomous decision of the banks. The article gives no reason for his resignation.
records.source_title: Qué dijo el presidente del Banco Central de El Salvador antes de renunciar (Diario El Mundo)
records.quote: asistió el jueves pasado al llamado de una comisión de la Asamblea Legislativa

records.summary: HaitiLibre reported that the Senate's Economy and Finance commission summoned Charles Castel, governor of the Banque de la République d'Haïti, together with Ronald Baudin, Minister of Economy and Finance, to appear on Wednesday 1 June 2011. They were called to answer questions about new taxes of US$1.50 per incoming or outgoing money transfer and 5 cents per minute on incoming international calls.
records.source_title: Haiti - Economy : Ronald Baudin and Charles Castel will have to give explanation regarding taxes (HaitiLibre)

records.summary: The Shift News reported that Edward Scicluna stepped aside from his functions as governor of the Central Bank of Malta while facing criminal charges, and that deputy governor Alexander Demarco would replace him. It reports that Scicluna had insisted he would not resign and that a Tuesday cabinet meeting appeared to have reached a compromise with him; Prime Minister Robert Abela is quoted insisting on the presumption of innocence. The article says Scicluna keeps his salary, which it puts at 138,000 euros.
records.source_title: Edward Scicluna forced to step aside (The Shift News)
records.quote: Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Malta Alexander Demarco will replace Edward Scicluna as he faces criminal charges
